stem: An outbreak affects 200 residents in a closed population of 10,000. By the end of complete follow-up, 10 affected residents have died from the disease and the remaining cases have recovered. Which of the following is the case-fatality proportion for this outbreak?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This calculation relates disease deaths to the entire population and describes disease-specific mortality over the observation period. Case fatality instead uses the people with the disease as its denominator.
options.misconception: Uses the population mortality denominator for case fatality.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This calculation describes the fraction of residents affected during the outbreak. It counts cases rather than deaths and therefore does not measure fatal outcomes among affected people.
options.misconception: Counts outbreak cases rather than fatal outcomes among cases.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This calculation gives the proportion of cases that survived and recovered. Case fatality uses the ten deaths, rather than the 190 survivors, in the numerator.
options.misconception: Uses recovered survivors rather than deaths in the fatality numerator.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Case fatality is the proportion of people with the condition who die from it. Ten deaths among 200 cases gives 10/200, or 5%, with complete outcome follow-up.
options.misconception: No misconception: case fatality divides disease deaths by all cases.

options.label: E
options.explanation: The denominator must include all cases, including those who died. Dividing deaths by survivors alone changes the measure and overstates the fatality proportion among all affected residents.
options.misconception: Excludes deaths from the case denominator by counting survivors alone.

context:
Learning objective: Distinguish fatality among cases from mortality in the full population.

Case fatality is the proportion of people with the condition who die from it. Ten deaths among 200 cases gives 10/200, or 5%, with complete outcome follow-up.
